Initialize gene sets list

Source: R/initializeList.R
initializeList.Rd

Initialize a 'gsList' object from a dataframe with gene sets and enrichment scores and a gene sets database.

Usage

initializeList(geneSetsList, geneSetsDF = NULL, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

geneSetsList

A list containing the gene sets to be analyzed. The name of each element in the list should be a gene set and each element should contain the genes belonging to that gene set. Alternatively, the path to a GMT file with the gene sets (read with fgsea::gmtPathways()).

geneSetsDF

Optional data.frame with gene sets and enrichment scores that can be useful for downstream visualization (both for effect size and direction and if multiple conditions are analyzed). Should have a column named 'pathway' containing the gene sets and a column named 'enrichment_score' or 'NES' with the enrichment of each gene set. Optionally have a column named 'pval' or 'pvalue' with the p-value of each gene set; a 'nlog10pval' column with the -log10 transformed p-values is added automatically and is used by default by the plotting functions that summarize scores (e.g. 'plotHeatmap()'). p-values must lie between 0 and 1. A p-value of 0 is transformed as the smallest positive double (giving about 307.7) rather than infinity. Optionally have a column named 'source' indicating the source of each gene set. This allows for analysis of multi-conditional data throughout the entire workflow and is also supported by many plotting functions. If a gene-set was found in multiple conditions there should be multiple rows for the same 'pathway' indicating its respective source and corresponding enrichment_score. Each combination of 'pathway' and 'source' may appear only once. Any other numeric column is kept and can be plotted via the 'plotFrom' argument of the plotting functions. List columns (e.g. 'leadingEdge' from fgsea) are dropped. See the vignette for examples.

verbose

a logic indicating whether to print progress statements. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

'gsList' object with a gene sets dataframe and enrichment scores for each gene set.

Details

Gene sets without any gene are removed with a warning. Missing gene ids (NA or empty strings) are ignored.

Examples

gsListObject <- initializeList(geneSetsList = exampleGeneSets, geneSetsDF = exampleEnrichment)
#> Checking input...
#> 2 different sources found.
#> Input is valid. Initializing gsList object...
#> gsList object created with 11210 genes and 197 gene sets from 2 sources
#> Initialization of gsList object DONE
gsListObject
#> A gsList object with 197 gene sets from 2 source(s).
#> Metadata:
#>   n pathways: 197

# Gene sets can also be read from a GMT file
gmtFile <- tempfile(fileext = ".gmt")
writeLines(
  vapply(names(exampleGeneSets), function(name) {
    paste(c(name, "", exampleGeneSets[[name]]), collapse = "\t")
  }, character(1)),
  gmtFile
)
gsListObject <- initializeList(gmtFile, exampleEnrichment, verbose = FALSE)
